topSignals.title: Doomberg "Artificial Bloom": third coordinated short-seller narrative on BE scandium — market holds firm
topSignals.text: — Doomberg, one of the most widely-read financial newsletters on Substack, published "Artificial Bloom" on July 14, 2026, joining Hunterbrook (July 8, China supply-chain allegations) and Crossroads Capital (July 9 first report + July 14 second report "supply wall") in a third independent short-seller narrative against Bloom Energy's scandium sourcing. Doomberg's piece focuses on Bloom's structural dependence on Chinese scandium oxide: arguing that CEO KR Sridhar's repeated "no China supply chain" claims since February 2025 are inconsistent with trade data pointing to Hunan Oriental Scandium as Bloom's largest fuel-cell-grade scandium supplier. Bloom's July 9 8-K (filed in response to Hunterbrook) stated: "We have sufficient supply of scandium oxide to meet our current fuel cell demand and backlog, and our supply is not dependent on China." Despite three coordinated attacks across seven trading days, BE closed July 14 at approximately $243.40 (+4.2%) — the fourth consecutive session the stock has resisted the short thesis, signalling market fatigue ahead of Q2 earnings (July 28). topSignals.title: FERC Generation Adequacy Reports: 5 days out (July 20)
topSignals.text: — The six RTO/ISO informational reports mandated by FERC's June 18 Section 206 show-cause orders are due in 5 days. Each of the six grid operators must submit a report explaining how sufficient generation will be available to serve existing and new large loads (≥50 MW on ≥69 kV). These will be the first regulator-mandated public disclosures quantifying the firm-power gap in each US grid region — representing the most authoritative external upper-bound estimate of the addressable market for SOFC grid-bypass power. ISO-NE has sought a 90-day abeyance (filing deadline August 3 instead of July 20). All six operators face full tariff reform or show-cause justifications due August 17. FERC RM26-4 | RMI analysis | McGuireWoods

topSignals.title: Germany EnEfG Amendment: cabinet adopted June 24 — PUE compliance window doubles for new data centers
topSignals.text: — The German government adopted a draft amendment to the Energy Efficiency Act (EnEfG) on June 24, 2026. Key changes for data centers commissioned from July 2026: (a) the compliance period to achieve PUE ≤1.2 on a sustained annual-average basis is extended from 2 years to 4 years after the start of operations; (b) for existing data centers (commissioned before July 2026), the 2027 PUE target relaxes from 1.5 to 1.6, and the 2030 target eases from 1.3 to 1.4; (c) waste heat reuse requirements are confirmed: 10% ERF from July 2026, 15% from July 2027, 20% from July 2028. The amendment still requires Bundestag and Bundesrat approval; implementation is expected Q3/Q4 2026. For European SOFC deployments: the doubled compliance window reduces the urgency of high-efficiency on-site generation as a regulatory driver in the near term, but the waste-heat ERF targets keep SOFC CHP mode (up to 90% system efficiency with heat recovery) as a compliance-relevant technology. Orrick (April amendment overview) | Taylor Wessing | Pinsent Masons

items.text: EFCF proceedings: day 12 blackout — journal embargo confirmed — The 17th European SOFC & SOE Forum closed July 3 in Lucerne. As of July 15 (12 days post-conference, now exceeding the longest typical conference embargo window), no technical results from Elcogen (E3000 G2: stated ≥75% electrical / ≥90% CHP at 650°C), Ceres licensees (Doosan yield trajectory vs. 90% target), SolydEra, or Convion have appeared online. A 12-day post-conference blackout on all participants simultaneously is consistent with a formal journal submission embargo rather than delayed press release drafting. Expect results via efcf.com proceedings or company websites when the embargo lifts. Key pending items unchanged: (a) Elcogen E3000 G2 real-commercial efficiency, (b) Doosan yield trajectory beyond Q1 2026's 80%, (c) manufacturing cost per kW from ELCO I Tallinn vs. Bloom Fremont. EFCF 2026

lcoe.text: Germany EnEfG amendment: 4-year compliance window for new DCs — New European SOFC data center projects commissioned from July 2026 now have 4 years (until 2030) to reach PUE ≤1.2 rather than 2 years. This reduces the near-term competitive pressure to use SOFC in CHP mode specifically for regulatory compliance, but the ERF waste-heat reuse requirements (10% active now, 15% July 2027, 20% July 2028) still create a compliance pathway for SOFC CHP. Recommend modelling European SOFC deployments with 4-year ramp to full CHP mode — this affects the timing of heat-revenue credits in the LCOE model.

Scandium "supply wall" now has three independent voices — Hunterbrook, Crossroads Capital, and Doomberg have all published the same supply-chain thesis within 7 days. If BE management cannot provide auditable non-China scandium sourcing data on July 28, the capex stress scenario (+15–30% above base case) may need to be elevated to an alternative base case for Bloom-only LCOE scenarios. Maintain as sensitivity pending July 28 earnings.

FERC July 20 reports: extract firm-power gap data — When published, these six RTO/ISO informational filings will contain the first regulatory-body estimates of load (MW) that cannot be served on-grid within 5 years per region. Extract these figures immediately after July 20 publication to validate the SOFC addressable market upper bound.

Primary LCOE model update trigger: July 28 BE Q2 earnings (AH) — 13 days away. Five inputs to monitor: (a) manufacturing cost per kW at 2 GW Fremont run rate, (b) product gross margin vs. ~34% guidance, (c) scandium/supply-chain transparency and sourcing disclosure, (d) Project Jupiter and AEP Wyoming timeline updates, (e) EaaS $/MWh pricing from Nebius or Brookfield-financed deployments.
